q: Guest has an egg allergy. Which fall seasonal do you steer them away from?
why: First Fallen Leaf is shaken with egg white for the foam. The Great Pumpkin's foam is heavy cream, not egg.
src: SEASONAL[First Fallen Leaf].build: "El Charro Reposado tequila, butterscotch liqueur, orange juice, egg white, lemon juice & cane syrup." note: "Egg white — shaken to a foam." SEASONAL[The Great Pumpkin].build: "...heavy cream (cold foam)..." (no egg in Herbologist or Mystery Martini builds)

q: Guest asks what's in At The Orchard besides Tito's and ginger beer. You say:
a: Apple cider, lemon & hot honey syrup
why: "Tito's, apple cider, lemon and hot honey, topped with ginger beer — crisp fall cider with a warm honey kick."
src: SEASONAL[At The Orchard].build: "Tito's, apple cider, lemon, hot honey syrup & ginger beer."

q: Which seasonal do you pour tableside, in a martini glass?
why: Mystery Martini is the only seasonal you pour in front of the guest. Every other martini comes already poured by the bar.
src: SEASONAL[Mystery Martini].glass: "Martini glass — poured tableside" vs [The Great Pumpkin].glass: "Martini glass — poured by bar"; [Mo's Bloody Mary Martini].glass: "...poured by bar"; [The Herbologist].glass: "Coupe — poured by bar"

q: Which seasonal has a garnish you lightly torch at the table?
why: Only The Herbologist gets a flame: torch the thyme sprig tableside. Bring the torch when it's ordered.
src: SEASONAL[The Herbologist].garnish: "Cherry & thyme — the thyme is lightly torched at the table"; no other seasonal garnish mentions torching

q: Guest: "Something light and refreshing — nothing heavy." Which seasonal?
why: "Crisp fall cider, warm hot-honey, a ginger-beer bite. Easy and refreshing." The Herbologist is the other Light and refreshing pick.
src: DRINK_PITCH[Light and refreshing]: "At The Orchard, The Herbologist"; SEASONAL[At The Orchard].desc: "Crisp fall cider, warm hot-honey, a ginger-beer bite. Easy and refreshing."

q: Guest: "I'm a gin person — light and dry." Which seasonal?
why: "Botanical gin, ripe pear, bright lemon and a whisper of cardamom. Light and dry."
src: SEASONAL[The Herbologist].base: "Gin"; .desc: "Botanical gin, ripe pear, bright lemon and a whisper of cardamom. Light and dry."; DRINK_PITCH[Light and refreshing]: "At The Orchard, The Herbologist"

q: Guest wants "sweet and fruity." Which two seasonals are that lane?
w: The Great Pumpkin & First Fallen Leaf
why: Offer apricot (Last Summer Sunset) or the Mystery Martini. Mo Berry off the signature list is the third option.
src: DRINK_PITCH[Sweet and fruity]: "Last Summer Sunset, Mystery Martini, Mo Berry"

q: Guest: "I want something that tastes like fall — cozy." Which two seasonals?
a: The Great Pumpkin & First Fallen Leaf
w: At The Orchard & Forest Blackberry Spritz
why: Pumpkin pie in a glass, or butterscotch and citrus over reposado. The cider drink is pitched as light and refreshing, not cozy.
src: DRINK_PITCH[Fall and cozy]: "The Great Pumpkin, First Fallen Leaf"; DRINK_PITCH[Light and refreshing]: "At The Orchard, The Herbologist"

q: Guest: "Nothing with alcohol tonight." Besides Bud Zero, what do you pitch and at what price?
why: Ask their lane — citrus, berry, tropical or herbal — and ring the mocktail at $12.
src: DRINK_PITCH[Nothing with alcohol]: "Mo's Make-A-Mocktail ($12) or Bud Zero"; COCKTAILS[Mo's Make-A-Mocktail].note: "Ask the guest which lane: citrus, berry, tropical, herbal."

q: The Great Pumpkin rings at what before any add-ons?
why: The Great Pumpkin is $15 — the ala mode scoop is extra.
src: SEASONAL[The Great Pumpkin].p: "$15" [verified vs mos-app/index.html COCKTAILS]

q: Which seasonal is built with egg white?
why: First Fallen Leaf is shaken with egg white for the froth — flag it for egg allergies.
src: SEASONAL[First Fallen Leaf].build: "...orange juice, egg white, lemon juice & cane syrup." / .note: "Egg white — shaken to a foam." (no egg in Herbologist, Last Summer Sunset or Mystery Martini builds) [verified vs mos-app/index.html COCKTAILS]

q: Dairy-allergic guest wants a seasonal. Which one do you steer them off?
why: The Great Pumpkin's cold-foam cap is heavy cream — that's the dairy flag on the seasonal list.
src: SEASONAL[The Great Pumpkin].build: "...heavy cream (cold foam) & allspice dust." (no dairy listed in Newton's Law, Mystery Martini or At The Orchard builds) [verified vs mos-app/index.html COCKTAILS]

q: Guest has a nut allergy. Which seasonal do you flag?
why: Newton's Law uses toasted almond bitters — steer a nut-allergic guest elsewhere.
src: SEASONAL[Newton's Law].build: "Woodford Double Oak, fig puree & toasted almond bitters." (no nut ingredient in Red Rum, Herbologist or Spritz builds) [verified vs mos-app/index.html COCKTAILS]

q: What's the base spirit in Newton's Law?
why: "Double-oaked Woodford, jammy fig, toasted almond bitters — a spirit-forward sipper." Our other bourbon drinks are Buffalo Trace; don't mix them up.
src: SEASONAL[Newton's Law].build: "Woodford Double Oak, fig puree & toasted almond bitters." Wrongs: SIGNATURE[Mo's Manifest Manhattan].build "Angel's Envy Rye..."; SIGNATURE[Smoked Draft Old Fashioned].build "Buffalo Trace Bourbon..."; SEASONAL[Forest Blackberry Spritz].build "Juniper-infused Old Forester Rye..."

q: Which fall seasonal is built on gin?
why: "Hendricks gin, ripe pear, bright lemon, a whisper of cardamom — light and dry." It's the only gin seasonal.
src: SEASONAL[The Herbologist].base: "Gin"; build: "Hendricks gin, pear liqueur, lemon, cardamom bitters & simple syrup." Wrongs: At The Orchard base "Vodka"; Forest Blackberry Spritz base "Rye / bubbles"; Mystery Martini base "Vodka"

q: What's the base spirit in the Last Summer Sunset?
why: "Apricot-infused LALO Blanco, Select Aperitivo, apricot liqueur — sunset-sweet." Blanco, not reposado; reposado is First Fallen Leaf.
src: SEASONAL[Last Summer Sunset].build: "Apricot-infused LALO Blanco tequila, Select Aperitivo, apricot liqueur & sweet and sour." Wrongs: First Fallen Leaf "El Charro Reposado tequila"; Forest Blackberry Spritz "Juniper-infused Old Forester Rye"; Mo's Bloody Mary Martini "Jalapeño-infused Tito's"

q: Guest loves pear. Which fall seasonal do you pitch?
why: "Botanical gin, ripe pear, bright lemon and a whisper of cardamom." At The Orchard is apple cider, not pear.
src: SEASONAL[The Herbologist].build: "Hendricks gin, pear liqueur, lemon, cardamom bitters & simple syrup." SEASONAL[At The Orchard].build: "Tito's, apple cider..."

q: Which fall seasonal is finished with ginger beer?
why: "Crisp fall cider, warm hot-honey, a ginger-beer bite." Also called the Tito's Draft Mule — it comes in a mule mug.
src: SEASONAL[At The Orchard].build: "Tito's, apple cider, lemon, hot honey syrup & ginger beer." glass: "Specialty mule mug" note: "Also called the Tito's Draft Mule."

q: Which liqueur gives First Fallen Leaf its signature flavor?
why: "Butterscotch and citrus over reposado — the egg white makes it round and frothy." Peach is Mystery Martini; apricot is Last Summer Sunset.
src: SEASONAL[First Fallen Leaf].build: "El Charro Reposado tequila, butterscotch liqueur, orange juice, egg white, lemon juice & cane syrup." desc: "Butterscotch and citrus over reposado; the egg white makes it round and frothy."

q: Which fall seasonal is capped with a heavy-cream cold foam?
why: "Vanilla, pumpkin and warm spice under a cold-foam cap, dusted with allspice." First Fallen Leaf is frothy too, but that's egg white.
src: SEASONAL[The Great Pumpkin].build: "...heavy cream (cold foam) & allspice dust." garnish: "Cold foam and allspice dust"; SEASONAL[First Fallen Leaf].note: "Egg white — shaken to a foam."

q: Which fall seasonal is made with blanco tequila?
why: "Apricot-infused LALO Blanco — bright and sunset-sweet." First Fallen Leaf is tequila too, but it's El Charro Reposado.
src: SEASONAL[Last Summer Sunset].base: "Blanco tequila"; SEASONAL[First Fallen Leaf].base: "Reposado tequila"; Mo's Bloody Mary Martini base "Vodka"; Red Rum base "Rum"

q: What rim goes on Mo's Bloody Mary Martini?
why: Celery salt on half the martini glass, never a full rim.
src: SEASONAL[Mo's Bloody Mary Martini].glass: "Martini glass, celery-salt half rim — poured by bar"

q: Which seasonal is served in the specialty mule mug?
why: At The Orchard is the mule (Tito's, cider, ginger beer), also called the Tito's Draft Mule. Only seasonal in the mug.
src: SEASONAL[At The Orchard].glass: "Specialty mule mug"; build: "Tito's, apple cider, lemon, hot honey syrup & ginger beer."; note: "Also called the Tito's Draft Mule."

q: How is the Forest Blackberry Spritz served?
why: It's finished with Prosecco, so it's built over ice in a wine glass. No other seasonal is served that way.
src: SEASONAL[Forest Blackberry Spritz].glass: "Wine glass, over ice"; build: "...cane syrup & Prosecco."

q: You grab a frothy coupe at the bar with one bay leaf on top. What is it?
why: Bay leaf on egg-white foam is the First Fallen Leaf. The Herbologist coupe has cherry and thyme.
src: SEASONAL[First Fallen Leaf].glass: "Coupe — poured by bar"; garnish: "Bay leaf"; note: "Egg white — shaken to a foam."; COCKTAILS[Mo's Manifest Manhattan].garnish: "Two Luxardo cherries"

q: Which of these seasonals is served in a martini glass?
why: Great Pumpkin is a martini-glass drink with a cold-foam cap, poured by the bar. The others are coupe, snifter, Glencairn.
src: SEASONAL[The Great Pumpkin].glass: "Martini glass — poured by bar"; [The Herbologist].glass: "Coupe — poured by bar"; [Red Rum].glass: "Snifter glass"; [Newton's Law].glass: "Glencairn glass"

q: What tops The Great Pumpkin?
why: Heavy-cream cold foam dusted with allspice: 'pumpkin pie in a glass.' The vanilla foam is the Mo Berry, not this.
src: SEASONAL[The Great Pumpkin].garnish: "Cold foam and allspice dust"; build: "...heavy cream (cold foam) & allspice dust."; desc: "Pumpkin pie in a glass"; COCKTAILS[Mo Berry].garnish: "Vanilla cold foam, crushed vanilla wafer if stocked"

q: A guest orders the seasonal in the Glencairn. What do you ring it at?
why: That's Newton's Law at $20, the priciest seasonal. Red Rum is $19; Spritz and Bloody Mary Martini are $18.
src: SEASONAL[Newton's Law].glass: "Glencairn glass"; p: "$20"; [Red Rum].p: "$19"; [Forest Blackberry Spritz].p: "$18"; [Mo's Bloody Mary Martini].p: "$18"; [Last Summer Sunset]/[First Fallen Leaf]/[The Great Pumpkin]/[The Herbologist].p: "$15"

q: A whiskey drinker asks what's new. Which seasonal is in the Whiskey forward lane?
why: The Spritz is rye too, but it's pitched as Bubbly. Newton's Law is the sipper: double-oaked bourbon, fig, toasted almond.
src: DRINK_PITCH[Whiskey forward]: "Newton's Law, Smoked Draft Old Fashioned, Mo's Signature OF"; DRINK_PITCH[Bubbly]: "Forest Blackberry Spritz"; SEASONAL[Newton's Law].desc: "Spirit-forward double-oaked bourbon, jammy fig, toasted-almond spice. A sipper."

q: Guest: "I like Negronis — bittersweet and boozy." Which seasonal?
why: Red Rum is the Bittersweet / boozy lane: aged rum with Campari, Amaro Montenegro and pomegranate over bright citrus.
src: DRINK_PITCH[Bittersweet / boozy]: "Red Rum, Mo's Manifest Manhattan"; SEASONAL[Red Rum].desc: "Rich and bittersweet — aged rum with pomegranate, Campari and amaro over bright citrus."

q: Table wants a drink instead of dessert. Which seasonal fits that pitch?
why: Dessert drink lane: Coco Caramel Carajillo, Esso Affo, or The Great Pumpkin ala mode — add ice cream for $3.
src: DRINK_PITCH[Dessert drink]: "Coco Caramel Carajillo, Esso Affo, or The Great Pumpkin ala mode"; SEASONAL[The Great Pumpkin].note: "Make It Ala Mode (add ice cream) for $3."

q: Guest asks what Newton's Law is like. Your one-liner:
a: Double-oaked bourbon, jammy fig, toasted-almond spice — a sipper.
w: Aged rum with pomegranate, Campari and amaro over bright citrus.
Butterscotch and citrus over reposado — round and frothy.
Botanical gin, ripe pear, bright lemon, a whisper of cardamom.
why: Woodford Double Oak, fig puree and toasted almond bitters in a Glencairn. Sell it as a sipper.
src: SEASONAL[Newton's Law].desc: "Spirit-forward double-oaked bourbon, jammy fig, toasted-almond spice. A sipper."; .build: "Woodford Double Oak, fig puree & toasted almond bitters."; .glass: "Glencairn glass"

q: Guest asks what Last Summer Sunset tastes like. Your one-liner:
a: Apricot-forward and sweet, with a bittersweet aperitivo backbone.
w: Lemon-forward and bright, with a soft peach sweetness.
Juniper-kissed rye and dark blackberry, finished with Prosecco.
Butterscotch and citrus over reposado, round and frothy.
why: Apricot-infused LALO Blanco, Select Aperitivo and apricot liqueur — sweet up front, bittersweet behind it.
src: SEASONAL[Last Summer Sunset].desc: "Apricot-forward and sunset-sweet with a bittersweet aperitivo backbone."; .build: "Apricot-infused LALO Blanco tequila, Select Aperitivo, apricot liqueur & sweet and sour."

q: Guest asks what happens tableside with The Herbologist. You say:
a: The thyme garnish is lightly torched at the table.
w: It's poured tableside from the shaker.
A bay leaf is dropped in at the table.
It's smoked under a lid, then revealed.
why: Torched thyme is The Herbologist. Tableside pour is the Mystery Martini; bay leaf is First Fallen Leaf.
src: SEASONAL[The Herbologist].garnish: "Cherry & thyme — the thyme is lightly torched at the table"; SEASONAL[Mystery Martini].glass: "Martini glass — poured tableside"; SEASONAL[First Fallen Leaf].garnish: "Bay leaf"

q: Tequila guest wants something rich and frothy, not a margarita. Send:
why: El Charro Reposado, butterscotch liqueur, citrus and egg white shaken to a foam — "round and frothy."
src: SEASONAL[First Fallen Leaf].base: "Reposado tequila"; .desc: "Butterscotch and citrus over reposado; the egg white makes it round and frothy."; .note: "Egg white — shaken to a foam."

q: Tequila guest wants it light and fruity in a tall glass. Send:
why: Apricot-infused LALO Blanco in a Collins glass with a star anise — the fruity, tall tequila pick.
src: SEASONAL[Last Summer Sunset].base: "Blanco tequila"; .glass: "Collins glass"; .garnish: "Star anise"; DRINK_PITCH[Sweet and fruity]: "Last Summer Sunset, Mystery Martini, Mo Berry"

q: Guest: "Do you have a mule?" Which seasonal is your answer?
why: At The Orchard is also called the Tito's Draft Mule — cider, hot honey and ginger beer in a specialty mule mug.
src: SEASONAL[At The Orchard].note: "Also called the Tito's Draft Mule."; .glass: "Specialty mule mug"

q: A Great Pumpkin guest wants it more dessert-like. Your upsell and price:
a: Make it ala mode (add ice cream) for $3
w: Make it ala mode (add ice cream) for $5
Make it ala mode (add ice cream) for $4
why: "Make It Ala Mode for $3" — that's the Dessert drink lane pick. Ring the $3 add-on.
src: SEASONAL[The Great Pumpkin].note: "Make It Ala Mode (add ice cream) for $3."; DRINK_PITCH[Dessert drink]: "...or The Great Pumpkin ala mode"; SEASONAL[Mo's Bloody Mary Martini].note: "Add A Caviar Bump for $27."

q: Guest says 'make my Great Pumpkin ala mode.' What's the drink's total?
why: $15 base plus $3 for the ice cream — ring the add-on so the ticket matches the menu.
src: SEASONAL[The Great Pumpkin].p: "$15" + .note: "Make It Ala Mode (add ice cream) for $3." [verified vs mos-app/index.html COCKTAILS]

q: How much is the caviar bump on Mo's Bloody Mary Martini?
why: The caviar bump is $27 — more than the drink itself, so quote it clearly before ringing.
src: SEASONAL[Mo's Bloody Mary Martini].note: "Add A Caviar Bump for $27." (drink .p: "$18") [verified vs mos-app/index.html COCKTAILS]

q: Which seasonal rings at $19?
why: Red Rum is $19 — Zacapa, Pama, Campari and Montenegro in a snifter.
src: SEASONAL[Red Rum].p: "$19", .build: "Zacapa Rum, Pama liqueur, Campari, Amaro Montenegro...", .glass: "Snifter glass" (Spritz "$18", Newton's Law "$20", Bloody Mary Martini "$18") [verified vs mos-app/index.html COCKTAILS]

q: What does the Mystery Martini ring at?
why: Mystery Martini is $14, poured tableside — the only seasonal at that price.
src: SEASONAL[Mystery Martini].p: "$14", .glass: "Martini glass — poured tableside" ($13 = At The Orchard, $15 = Herbologist, $16 = Mo's Signature OF) [verified vs mos-app/index.html COCKTAILS]

q: What brings the heat in Mo's Bloody Mary Martini?
why: The vodka itself is jalapeño-infused — the heat is in the base, not a garnish you can leave off.
src: SEASONAL[Mo's Bloody Mary Martini].build: "Jalapeño-infused Tito's..." (wrongs are real: hot honey syrup = At The Orchard; cardamom bitters = The Herbologist; toasted almond bitters = Newton's Law) [verified vs mos-app/index.html COCKTAILS]

q: Guest wants a dessert drink off the seasonal list. What do you pitch?
why: Dessert-drink lane: Coco Caramel Carajillo, Esso Affo, or The Great Pumpkin ala mode — the pumpkin is the seasonal pick.
src: DRINK_PITCH[Dessert drink]: "Coco Caramel Carajillo, Esso Affo, or The Great Pumpkin ala mode" [verified vs mos-app/index.html DRINK_PITCH]

q: Which is NOT in the Red Rum?
why: Red Rum is Zacapa with Pama, Campari and Amaro Montenegro over citrus. Select Aperitivo is the Last Summer Sunset's bitter.
src: SEASONAL[Red Rum].build: "Zacapa Rum, Pama liqueur, Campari, Amaro Montenegro, orange juice, lemon juice & cane syrup." SEASONAL[Last Summer Sunset].build: "...Select Aperitivo..."

q: Which two fall seasonals are both built on Tito's?
a: At The Orchard & Mo's Bloody Mary Martini
w: The Great Pumpkin & Mo's Bloody Mary Martini
why: At The Orchard is plain Tito's; the Bloody Mary Martini is jalapeño-infused Tito's. Mystery Martini and Great Pumpkin use Pearl vodkas.
src: SEASONAL[At The Orchard].build: "Tito's, apple cider..."; SEASONAL[Mo's Bloody Mary Martini].build: "Jalapeño-infused Tito's..."; SEASONAL[Mystery Martini].build: "Pearl Lemon vodka..."; SEASONAL[The Great Pumpkin].build: "Pearl Vanilla Vodka..."

q: Which vodka is the base of the Mystery Martini?
why: "Pearl Lemon vodka, peach and Luxardo cherry liqueurs, muddled lemon — bright and lemon-forward." 360 Lemon is the Cosmo, not this.
src: SEASONAL[Mystery Martini].build: "Pearl Lemon vodka, peach liqueur, Luxardo cherry liqueur, triple sec, dry vermouth, fresh muddled lemon." SIGNATURE[Mo's Cosmo].build: "360 Lemon Vodka..."

q: The rye in the Forest Blackberry Spritz is infused with what?
why: "The rye is infused with juniper — the gin botanical — so it reads piney and peppery against the blackberry." Blackberry comes from puree, not the infusion.
src: SEASONAL[Forest Blackberry Spritz].build: "Juniper-infused Old Forester Rye, blackberry puree..." note: "Juniper (the gin botanical) is piney and woody — bright lemon/orange with a peppery spice."

q: Which fall seasonal has Licor 43 in the build?
why: "Pearl Vanilla Vodka and Licor 43 with pumpkin puree and pumpkin pie syrup — pumpkin pie in a glass."
src: SEASONAL[The Great Pumpkin].build: "Pearl Vanilla Vodka, Licor 43 vanilla, pumpkin puree, pumpkin pie syrup, heavy cream (cold foam) & allspice dust." (no Licor 43 in Newton's Law, First Fallen Leaf or Red Rum builds)

q: Which bitters finish Newton's Law?
why: "The toasted almond bitters add a warm, nutty spice to the jammy fig." Cardamom bitters are The Herbologist.
src: SEASONAL[Newton's Law].build: "Woodford Double Oak, fig puree & toasted almond bitters." SEASONAL[The Herbologist].build: "...cardamom bitters..."; SIGNATURE[Mo's Signature OF].build: "...Angostura & orange bitters..."

q: Which fall seasonal has dry vermouth in it?
why: "A true martini build — Pearl Lemon vodka, peach and cherry liqueurs, triple sec, dry vermouth — poured tableside." The other martinis carry no vermouth.
src: SEASONAL[Mystery Martini].build: "Pearl Lemon vodka, peach liqueur, Luxardo cherry liqueur, triple sec, dry vermouth, fresh muddled lemon." glass: "Martini glass — poured tableside" (no vermouth in Bloody Mary Martini, Great Pumpkin or Herbologist builds)

q: What's the base spirit in the Red Rum?
why: "Aged Zacapa rum with pomegranate, Campari and amaro over bright citrus — rich and bittersweet." Diplomatico is Mo Berry; Hard Truth is the Carajillo.
src: SEASONAL[Red Rum].build: "Zacapa Rum, Pama liqueur, Campari, Amaro Montenegro, orange juice, lemon juice & cane syrup." SIGNATURE[Mo Berry].build: "Diplomatico Rum..."; DESSERT[Coco Caramel Carajillo].build: "...Hard Truth toasted coconut rum..."; SIGNATURE[Mo's Manifest Manhattan].build "Angel's Envy Rye..."

q: What gets muddled into Mo's Bloody Mary Martini?
why: "Jalapeño-infused Tito's, lime, olive juice and muddled cherry tomatoes, topped with cracked pepper and basil oil." The jalapeño is in the vodka, not muddled.
src: SEASONAL[Mo's Bloody Mary Martini].build: "Jalapeño-infused Tito's, pinch of sea salt, lime, olive juice, muddled cherry tomatoes, topped with fresh cracked pepper & basil oil." Wrongs: Mystery Martini "fresh muddled lemon"; Mo's Signature OF "muddled cherry & orange"

q: Which fall seasonal uses sweet and sour in the build?
why: "Apricot LALO Blanco, Select Aperitivo and apricot liqueur, lengthened with sweet and sour." Herbologist and Spritz use lemon plus simple or cane syrup.
src: SEASONAL[Last Summer Sunset].build: "Apricot-infused LALO Blanco tequila, Select Aperitivo, apricot liqueur & sweet and sour." The Herbologist "lemon... & simple syrup"; Forest Blackberry Spritz "lemon, cane syrup"

q: Guest asks: "Is the Forest Blackberry Spritz a bourbon drink?" You answer:
a: No — it's juniper-infused Old Forester Rye
why: "It's rye, not bourbon — juniper-infused Old Forester Rye with blackberry, lemon, cane syrup and Prosecco." Woodford Double Oak is Newton's Law.
src: SEASONAL[Forest Blackberry Spritz].base: "Rye / bubbles"; build: "Juniper-infused Old Forester Rye, blackberry puree, lemon, cane syrup & Prosecco." SEASONAL[Newton's Law].build: "Woodford Double Oak..."

q: Which fall seasonal has Campari in it?
why: "Campari and Amaro Montenegro give the Red Rum its bittersweet backbone." Last Summer Sunset's bitter is Select Aperitivo — less bitter than Campari.
src: SEASONAL[Red Rum].build: "Zacapa Rum, Pama liqueur, Campari, Amaro Montenegro, orange juice, lemon juice & cane syrup." SEASONAL[Last Summer Sunset].note: "Select Aperitivo is a Venetian bitter... less bitter than Campari."

q: Newton's Law goes in which glass?
why: Spirit-forward bourbon sipper, so it's the Glencairn. Not a rocks glass.
src: SEASONAL[Newton's Law].glass: "Glencairn glass"; desc: "Spirit-forward double-oaked bourbon... A sipper."

q: Which seasonal comes out in a snifter?
why: Snifter means Red Rum: rich, bittersweet aged rum.
src: SEASONAL[Red Rum].glass: "Snifter glass"; desc: "Rich and bittersweet — aged rum..."; vs [Newton's Law].glass: "Glencairn glass"; [First Fallen Leaf].glass: "Coupe — poured by bar"; [Last Summer Sunset].glass: "Collins glass"

q: What's the garnish on The Herbologist?
why: Cherry and a thyme sprig. The thyme gets lightly torched at the table so the guest smells it first.
src: SEASONAL[The Herbologist].garnish: "Cherry & thyme — the thyme is lightly torched at the table"

q: What garnish sits on the Glencairn-glass seasonal?
why: That's Newton's Law. The Fig Newton cookie ties to the fig puree in the glass.
src: SEASONAL[Newton's Law].glass: "Glencairn glass"; garnish: "A Fig Newton cookie"; build: "Woodford Double Oak, fig puree & toasted almond bitters."

q: What's the garnish on the Forest Blackberry Spritz?
why: Mint bundle plus a lemon wedge. The lemon matches the citrus in the build.
src: SEASONAL[Forest Blackberry Spritz].garnish: "Mint bundle & lemon wedge"; build: "Juniper-infused Old Forester Rye, blackberry puree, lemon..."

q: Last Summer Sunset goes in which glass?
why: It's the tall one, a Collins. In a mug or snifter, it was built wrong.
src: SEASONAL[Last Summer Sunset].glass: "Collins glass"

q: A guest asks what the star-shaped garnish is. Which seasonal did they order?
why: Star anise on the Last Summer Sunset. Say it reads like sweet black licorice against the apricot.
src: SEASONAL[Last Summer Sunset].garnish: "Star anise"; note: "Star anise reads like sweet black licorice."

q: What's the garnish on the Red Rum?
why: Dried orange and one Luxardo cherry on the snifter. The orange echoes the Campari and OJ in the build.
src: SEASONAL[Red Rum].garnish: "Dried orange & Luxardo cherry"; build: "Zacapa Rum, Pama liqueur, Campari, Amaro Montenegro, orange juice..."

q: What garnish goes in the Mystery Martini?
why: Drop one cherry in after your tableside pour. It's the finish to the show.
src: SEASONAL[Mystery Martini].garnish: "A dropped cherry"; glass: "Martini glass — poured tableside"

q: Guest asks what Select Aperitivo is in the Last Summer Sunset. You say:
a: A Venetian bitter — more herbaceous than Aperol, less bitter than Campari.
w: Bitter orange peel and grapefruit, around since 1860.
A pomegranate liqueur, like the Pama in the Red Rum.
Herbal-cola and root beer with warm spice.
why: Select sits between Aperol and Campari — the easy way to sell it to a spritz drinker.
src: SEASONAL[Last Summer Sunset].note: "Select Aperitivo is a Venetian bitter (est. 1920) — more herbaceous than Aperol, less bitter than Campari."; wrongs from SEASONAL[Red Rum].note (Campari, Montenegro) and .build/.desc (Pama liqueur / pomegranate)

q: A Mo's Bloody Mary Martini guest wants to go big. The add-on:
why: "Add A Caviar Bump for $27" — the savory martini is the one with the caviar upsell. Get the price right on the ticket.

q: Which bourbon on the regular list is port-finished?
why: Angel's Envy is the port-finished bourbon — round, vanilla, dried fruit, $16. Good pick for a guest who likes something a little sweeter.
src: SPIRITS[Bourbon (2 oz unless noted)][Angel's Envy]: "$16 — Port-finished bourbon; round, vanilla, dried fruit"; [Basil Hayden's] "Light, easy, softer bourbon"; [Elijah Craig Small Batch] "Oak, vanilla, balanced"; [Maker's 46] "Richer Maker's, more vanilla and oak"

q: Which is the strongest beer on the list?
why: Space Dust is 8.2% — strongest on the list, grapefruit, mango and pine. Warn a guest who wants a session beer; All Day IPA is the easy-drinking one.
src: BEER[Elysian Space Dust]: "8.2% — India Pale Ale — Strongest beer on the list; grapefruit, mango, pine"; [Metazoa Hoppopotamus IPA] "7.0%"; [Centerpoint Blood Orange IPA] "5.2%"; [Founder's All Day IPA] "4.7% — Session IPA"

q: What's the story on the Prime 47 Blend?
a: A Bardstown single barrel our Prime 47 Carmel bar manager tasted at the source and bought exclusively
w: A Buffalo Trace private barrel picked for the Smoked Old Fashioned
A Bardstown collab finished in Goose Island stout barrels
A Bardstown rye finished in cherry-oak barrels
why: "You're pouring from a barrel our own team chose in Bardstown, Kentucky." $30. Goose Island and WV Great Barrel are the other Bardstown collabs.
src: spirits.json spirits[Bardstown & Specialty][Prime 47 Blend]: "$30" / "Bardstown single barrel picked by OUR people: the Prime 47 Carmel bar manager toured Bardstown, Kentucky, tasted at the source, and bought one exclusive barrel"

q: Which Bardstown pour's cooperage was built to help rebuild a county after a 2016 flood?
why: The WV Great Barrel Co. cooperage was built to help rebuild Greenbrier County after the 2016 flood. Rye blend, cherry-oak barrels, 110 proof — cherry, vanilla, rye spice. $35.
src: SPIRITS[Bardstown & Specialty][West Virginia Great Barrel]: "$35 — Bardstown collab with the WV Great Barrel Co. cooperage — rye blend finished in infrared-toasted cherry-oak barrels, 110 proof. The cooperage was built to help rebuild Greenbrier County, WV after the 2016 flood."

q: At the greet, right after you introduce yourself and your back server, what do you ask?
a: First time? Celebrating? Allergies? Wine list?
w: Features, soup of the day, cut specials
why: Those four questions set up the whole night — then point them to cocktails, beer, wine, and whiskey. Keep it warm and short.
src: SERVICE.flow[Greet]: "Introduce yourself and your back server." / "Ask first time, celebration, allergies, and whether they want the wine list." / "Keep it warm and short."

q: What is the back server's very first touch on a new table?
a: B&B plates, after the front greets
w: Dessert menus and the dessert talk
why: Busser drops water, front greets, then the back lays B&B plates. The back only shows up with a reason to be there.
src: SERVICE.house.mise[Preset before the food ever lands]: "B&B plates go down after the front greets — the back server's first touch on the table." / SERVICE.house.back: "Greet only when you have a reason to be there. Drop B&B plates after the front greets."

q: Two to five minutes after entrees land, what exactly do you say?
w: "This is going down here for your convenience."
"Great question — let me find out for you."
why: That is the house checkback line. A halfhearted answer means something is wrong — pry gently and fix it now.
src: SERVICE.house.front: "Entree checkback at 2-5 minutes: 'Is everything tasting perfect for us?' A halfhearted answer means something is wrong — pry gently and fix it."

q: At the entree checkback the guest gives a flat 'it's fine.' What do you do?
a: Pry gently and fix it immediately
w: Ask again when you clear the plates
Drop the check with dessert to speed the exit
Note it and bring a dessert menu
why: A halfhearted answer means something is wrong. Problems caught at checkback mean fewer comps and happier exits.
src: SERVICE.house.front: "A halfhearted answer means something is wrong — pry gently and fix it." / "Problems caught at checkback mean fewer comps and happier exits." / SERVICE.flow[Course checkbacks]: "If the answer sounds weak, fix it immediately."

q: Your entrees land at the 24-minute mark. Where does that sit against the standard?
a: Over the 22 target, under the 25 max
why: Entrees aim for about 22 minutes with 25 the maximum goal. Watch the ticket and communicate a delay before the guest has to ask.
src: SERVICE.trainer.parts[Four-Course Service & Timing]: "Entrées — Approximately 22 minutes; maximum goal 25 minutes." / "communicating delays before the guest has to ask."

q: Soups and salads should hit the table within how many minutes?
why: Soup/salad is the fastest course in the building — two to five minutes, with bread and the pepper mill riding along.
src: SERVICE.trainer.parts[Four-Course Service & Timing]: "Soup / Salad — 2 – 5 minutes." / SERVICE.house.mise[Soup, salad and bread]: "Bread ALWAYS comes with soups and salads... Offer freshly cracked pepper EVERY time"

q: To keep coursing clean in Toast, soups/salads and entrees get rung…
w: Entrees only after the salads clear
With the apps, entrees on a second ticket
Entrees first, S&S as a follow-up
why: A time gap between the S&S and entree ring is how coursing gets confused. One ring, the kitchen paces it.
src: SERVICE.house.barsteps: "Ring S&S and entrees together — no time gap, that is how coursing gets confused."

q: Why does the back server tell the front the moment the apps are cleared?
a: So the front can send the full order
w: So the front can drop the check
So the manager can open the wine
So expo can hold the entrees
why: Apps cleared is the signal — the front sends the full order and the kitchen clock starts on the next course.
src: SERVICE.house.back: "Run and clear apps... Tell the front apps are cleared so they can send the full order."

q: The best moment to ask about a second bottle or another round is…
a: Right after the salad course clears
w: At the greet, with the wine list
When you drop the dessert menu
why: Salad cleared means glasses are getting low and entrees are coming — the natural moment to move them to another bottle.
src: SERVICE.house.front: "Salad course cleared = the moment to ask about a bottle or another round." / SERVICE.flow[Course checkbacks]: "After salad or soup clears, ask about another round or a second bottle."

q: When do the features go over at a table?
a: Before you take the full order
why: Offer to take the full order and course it out — but the features get pitched first, so the guest can choose them.
src: SERVICE.house.front: "Offer to take the full order and course it out — guests may assume everything comes at once. Features go over before the full order."

q: A shrimp cocktail is on the way. When does the cocktail fork hit the table?
w: Dropped right after the plate lands
Set when the shells are cleared
why: The cocktail fork goes down before the plate — never after, never with. Presetting the next course is the whole game.
src: service.json house.mise[Preset before the food ever lands]: "The COCKTAIL FORK goes down before the plate arrives — never after, never with."

q: Which item does NOT belong on the seasonal oyster setup?
why: Oysters get oyster fork, Tabasco, Zesta crackers, cocktail forks and hot water for the dry-ice smoke — NO tongs.
src: service.json house.mise[Starters]: "Oysters: oyster fork, Tabasco, Zesta crackers, cocktail forks, and hot water for the dry-ice smoke. NO tongs."

q: Which side goes out with tongs instead of a serving spoon?
why: Tongs ride with asparagus (hollandaise on the side) and truffle fries. Nearly every other side is a serving spoon.
src: service.json house.mise[Sides]: "Tongs: grilled asparagus (hollandaise on the side), truffle fries (ketchup on the side)." / "Serving spoon: both mashed potatoes, risotto, creamed corn, creamed spinach, lobster mac, jalapeno au gratin, Brussels sprouts, truffle cauliflower."

q: When do the B&B plates go down?
w: With the waters, before the greet
With the soup or salad drop
why: B&Bs go down after the front greets — it is the back server's first touch on the table.
src: service.json house.mise[Preset before the food ever lands]: "B&B plates go down after the front greets — the back server's first touch on the table." / house.back: "Drop B&B plates after the front greets."

q: Which course is served from the guest's RIGHT?
why: Serve from the left, clear from the right — soup and hot beverages are the exception and go in from the right.
src: service.json trainer.parts[3. Core Dining-Room Service Standards]: "Serve from the left and clear from the right." / "Soup and hot beverages are served from the right." / trainer.parts[4]: "Salads are served from the left."

q: Desserts are ordered. How do you mark the table?
why: Mark with B&Bs and dessert spoons the moment desserts are ordered — teaspoon on the right, B&Bs if the table is sharing.
src: service.json house.mise[Desserts and after-dinner]: "Mark the table with B&Bs and dessert spoons the moment desserts are ordered." / "Teaspoon on the right. B&B plates if the table is sharing."

q: Clearing salads — what is the one-trip move?
a: Everything on the tray, knives and correct silverware down, crumb
w: Clear, then come back with the pepper mill
Clear the salads, leave knives until entrees land
Stack the plates tableside, then crumb
why: Clear and mark in one trip: everything onto the tray, correct silverware down, crumb again. Never stack plates at the table.
src: service.json house.back: "Clear salads and mark the table in one trip: everything onto the tray, then knives and correct silverware down, crumb again." / house.isaacs: "no stacking plates tableside"

q: Captain's Pad: what fills the header before you take a word of the order?
a: Table number top-left, guest count top-right
w: Guest count top-left, table number top-right
Your name top-left, seat count top-right
Table number top-left, seat 1's drink top-right
why: Header first, every ticket. Anyone who picks up that pad knows the table and the count before reading a seat.
src: CAPTAIN.rules[Fill the header first]: "TABLE # top-left, # OF GUESTS top-right. Do it before you take a word of the order."

q: Where is seat 1 on the pad, and which way do you count from it?
a: Usually faces the front door, then clockwise
w: Usually faces the kitchen, then clockwise
Usually faces the front door, then counter-clockwise
Usually faces the bar, then counter-clockwise
why: Seat numbers are the pivot point system — a runner who has never met the table drops the right plate without asking.
src: CAPTAIN.rules[Number the seats like the floor plan]: "Seat 1 usually faces the front door; number clockwise from there."

q: On the Captain's Pad, what does a circled seat number mean?
a: A woman sits there — served first
w: An allergy lives at that seat
That seat is holding the check
A first-time guest at that seat
why: The single most important mark on the pad. Whoever runs the tray serves ladies first and drops each plate on the right person.
src: CAPTAIN.rules[Circle the women]: "Circle every woman's seat number. That is how the runner serves ladies first and drops each plate on the right person — the single most important mark on the pad." / CAPTAIN.rules[Allergies...]: allergies are written on the row, not circled.

q: Read the row: "Seat ◯3 · FO · Salm (broiled) · Chardonnay". What goes to seat 3?
a: A woman: French onion, broiled salmon, Chardonnay
w: A woman: Caesar no anchovies, blackened salmon, Chardonnay
A man: French onion, broiled salmon, Chardonnay
A woman: French onion, blackened salmon, Chablis
why: Circle = woman, FO = Baked French Onion, and the note says broiled instead of the default blackening.
src: CAPTAIN.example.lines[Seat ◯3]: "FO · Salm (broiled) · Chardonnay" / example.reads: "Seat 3 is a woman: French onion, salmon broiled not blackened, Chardonnay." / CAPTAIN.ss: "FO — Baked French Onion"; steaks: "Salm — Blackened Creole Salmon (say if broiled/plain)"

q: A guest with an entree wants the lobster bisque instead of the soup of the day. Pad mark and charge?
a: Bisq — $4 up from the comp soup
w: Bisq — no charge, it is comp with entrees
why: SD is the complimentary soup with entrees; bisque or French onion is a $4 upcharge. Write Bisq so it rings right.
src: CAPTAIN.ss: "Bisq — Lobster Bisque ($4 up from the comp soup)"; "SD — Soup of the Day (the comp soup with entrees)"; "FO — Baked French Onion" / BOOK[Day 2] Soups: "it comes complimentary with entrees — or the guest can upcharge $4 to lobster bisque or baked French onion."

q: Decode the pad line "6 Fil MR +Osc".
a: 6 oz filet, medium rare, add crab Oscar
w: 6 oz filet, medium, add crab Oscar
6 oz FarBuckle filet, medium rare, add crab Oscar
10 oz filet, medium rare, add crab Oscar
why: Size goes before the cut, temp after it, add-ons with a plus. Fil is the plain filet; FB would be the FarBuckle.
src: CAPTAIN.steaks: "6 / 10 — the size in oz — write it before the cut"; "Fil — Filet Mignon (the default steak — '6 Fil MR')"; "FB — FarBuckle Filet" / temps: "MR — Medium Rare"; "M — Medium" / addons: "+Osc — Crab Oscar ($14)"

q: A guest orders a filet well done. Which mark should ride next to the WD on the pad?
why: Offer to butterfly every well-done filet — it cooks faster and comes out juicier. The guest hears you protecting their dinner.
src: CAPTAIN.temps: "bf — butterfly it — offer on any well-done filet" / CAPTAIN.mods: "bf — butterfly (well-done filets)" / FLOW[Menu wrap / order]: "Mention steak temps and that well-done filets should be butterflied."

q: Seat 4 tells you they have a nut allergy. What happens on the pad and beyond it?
a: Write it on seat 4's row, ring it in, tell back server, expo, chef, and a manager
w: Circle seat 4 and tell the chef when the entrees fire
Write it in the SIDES lines so the whole table's order carries it
Write it on seat 4's row and hand the white copy to your back server
why: Never let an allergy live only on the pad. It gets rung in and said out loud to four people, every time.
src: CAPTAIN.rules[Allergies get written ON the seat and rung in]: "Note the allergy right on that seat's row, ring it in, and tell the back server, expo, chef, and a manager. Never let it live only on the pad." / example.lines[Seat 4]: "NUT ALLERGY, rung in"

q: A guest at another team's table has an empty plate and no fork. Isaac's rule?
a: Handle it — every guest is everybody's guest, that beats sections
w: Flag their front server and keep moving
Tell the busser for that section and keep moving
Note it for your back server and finish your own table first
why: Hospitality is a lifestyle you do not turn off. Empty plates, missing silverware, running food — ours, no matter whose section.
src: HOUSE.isaacs: "Every guest is everybody's guest. Hospitality is a lifestyle you do not turn off. When one of OUR guests needs something, that beats sections and roles — empty plates, missing silverware, running food, escorting to the restroom."

q: Which pair is the house standard for direction of service?
a: Serve from the left, clear from the right
w: Serve from the right, clear from the left
Serve and clear from the right
Serve and clear from the left
why: Left in, right out — with soups and hot beverages as the exception, served from the right.
src: TRAINER.parts[3. Core Dining-Room Service Standards].items: "Serve from the left and clear from the right." / "Soup and hot beverages are served from the right."

q: Two women at the table ordered salads; the man ordered French onion. Who gets served first?
a: The man — hot soups go first regardless of gender
w: Nobody first — all three land together
why: Hot soup is the one thing that outranks ladies-first. It cools and skins while a salad waits.
src: TRAINER.parts[3. Core Dining-Room Service Standards].items: "Ladies are served first under normal service." / "Hot soups are served first regardless of gender." / TRAINER soup-salad section: "Hot soups take priority and are served first regardless of gender."

q: A guest says "thank you" at the table. Which reply is the Mo's way?
why: Never "no problem." "My pleasure" or "absolutely" — the words are the uniform of the sentence.
src: BOOK[Start Here] How we speak: "Never 'no problem.' Say 'my pleasure' or 'absolutely.'" ("Great question — let me find out for you" is the 'I don't know' replacement; "pardon my reach" is HOUSE.isaacs personal-space line)

q: After introducing you and your back server, what do you ASK at the greet?
a: First time, celebration, allergies, wine list
w: Sides and enhancements: Oscar, Steak 47, lobster tail
Dessert, after-dinner drinks, port, espresso martinis
why: Those four questions set up the whole table — the specials and soup get TOLD in the menu wrap, not asked.
src: SERVICE.flow[Greet]: "Introduce yourself and your back server. Ask first time, celebration, allergies, and whether they want the wine list."

q: Who drops the soup/salad course and introduces themselves at that drop?
why: Busser waters, front greets and takes drinks/apps/soup-salad, then the back drops the soup or salad and says hello right there.
src: SERVICE.flow[Soup, salad & bread]: "then the BACK server drops the soup or salad and introduces themselves right there"

q: Who gets waters on the table first?
why: The busser greets with water before the front server even walks up.
src: SERVICE.flow[Soup, salad & bread]: "busser greets with water, front server greets and gets drinks plus apps and soup/salad"

q: Bread service lands…
a: With the soup and salad course — always
why: Bread ALWAYS rides with soups and salads — French bread with garlic-salt butter plus the whipped butter.
src: SERVICE.flow[Soup, salad & bread]: "Bread ALWAYS comes with soups and salads — French bread with garlic-salt butter, plus smooth whipped butter."

q: Cracked pepper gets offered…
a: At every soup and salad drop — bring the mill
why: Bring the mill and offer it every single time you drop a soup or salad — don't wait to be asked.
src: SERVICE.mise[Soup, salad and bread]: "Offer freshly cracked pepper EVERY time after you drop a soup or a salad. Bring the mill; do not wait to be asked."

q: The course order is…
why: Appetizers (skippable), then soups and salads, then entrées — it never changes.
src: SERVICE.flow[Soup, salad & bread]: "Course order never changes: appetizers (skippable), then soups/salads, then entrees."

q: Who opens and pours wine bottles at the table?
a: A MANAGER — every bottle, every time
w: The front server who sold it
why: The front server sets the glasses; a manager opens and pours the bottle at the table, every time.
src: SERVICE.flow[Drinks first]: "the front server sets the glasses, and a MANAGER opens and pours the bottle at the table — every time"

q: Entrée ticket time runs…
why: Aim for 22, never past 25 — course it, don't stack it. The old 22–27 line is retired.
src: SERVICE.flow[Before you walk up]: "entrees 22 with 25 the max" / rows[Entrées]: "Approximately 22 minutes; maximum goal 25 minutes."

q: The entrée checkback happens…
a: 2–5 minutes after entrées hit the table
why: Two bites in: 'Is everything tasting perfect for us?' A halfhearted answer means something is wrong — fix it now.
src: SERVICE.flow[Course checkbacks]: "Entree checkback is 2-5 minutes after entrees hit: 'Is everything tasting perfect for us?'"

q: What bread comes out with soups and salads?
a: French bread with garlic-salt butter and whipped butter
w: Crostini with whipped goat cheese and honey
Pretzel buns with smoked garlic aioli
why: Bread ALWAYS rides with the soup or salad course — and offer fresh cracked pepper every time.
src: SERVICE.flow[Soup, salad & bread]: "Bread ALWAYS comes with soups and salads — French bread with garlic-salt butter, plus smooth whipped butter."

q: Correct ticket timing?
a: Starters 5–12 (15 max); soups/salads 2–5; entrees 22 target / 25 max; desserts within 7
w: Starters 7–12; soups/salads 5–10; entrees 30 target / 35 max; desserts within 10
Starters 10–15; soups/salads 2–5; entrees 25 target / 30 max; desserts within 5
Starters 5–12; soups/salads 7–12; entrees 20 target / 22 max; desserts within 12
why: Know the clock so you can flag a late ticket before the guest asks. Seafood towers are the exception on starters.
src: service.json trainer.parts[3].items: "7 – 12 minutes. Seafood towers are the exception" / "2 – 5 minutes" / "Approximately 22 minutes; maximum goal 25 minutes" / "Within 7 minutes" — starters updated to the current 5–12 (15 max) standard per the task's timing rule

q: What is bread service at Mo's?
a: French bread with garlic-salt butter plus whipped butter — always with soups and salads
w: Brioche with garlic-salt butter, on request
Crostini with whipped butter, with starters
why: Bread ALWAYS comes with the soup or salad course — French bread, garlic-salt butter and smooth whipped butter.
src: service.json flow[4][1][1]: "Bread ALWAYS comes with soups and salads — French bread with garlic-salt butter, plus smooth whipped butter"

q: A table is celebrating a birthday. What do they get?
a: A lit sparkler plus a comp Celebration Sundae or Mo's Cookie — no singing required
w: A comp Mo's Sundae with a sparkler
A comp Celebration Cake slice and the staff sings
A comp Bailey's Creme Brulee with a candle
why: Every celebration gets a sparkler. The comp is the Celebration Sundae or a Mo's Cookie — NOT the $15 Mo's Sundae. Pull the spent sparkler with a black linen.
src: desserts.json desserts[Celebration Sundae]: "The free one, and it is NOT the Mo's Sundae ... The other option is a comp Mo's Cookie ... We do NOT sing — we light a SPARKLER"

q: A guest sits down at the bar top. The greet has to happen within…
why: Sixty seconds to greet, water and menus inside two minutes, first drink inside five. The bar runs the same religion, faster.
src: SERVICE.house.barsteps: "Greet within 60 SECONDS of a guest sitting at the bar top. Water + menus inside 2 minutes ('still, sparkling, or regular ice water?'). First drink inside 5 minutes."

q: Desserts are expected on the table within…
why: Within seven minutes — and on busy nights the check is already printed and rides down with the desserts.
src: SERVICE.trainer.parts[Four-Course Service & Timing]: "Desserts — Within 7 minutes." / SERVICE.house.back: "Have the check ready to drop WITH desserts on busy nights"

q: Which starter is the exception to the appetizer ticket-time window?
why: Appetizer timing has one carve-out: the towers. Set the guest's expectation when they order one.
src: SERVICE.trainer.parts[Four-Course Service & Timing]: "Appetizers — 7 – 12 minutes. Seafood towers are the exception." / SERVICE.house.barsteps: "Apps 7-12, towers excepted."

q: Which soup/salad item is the exception to the 2–5 minute window?
why: The French onion is the one soup/salad item allowed to run past the window — its provolone is melted in the broiler, so set the expectation.
src: SERVICE.house.barsteps: "S&S in 2-5 (French onion is the exception)." / FOOD[Baked French Onion]: "provolone melted in the broiler"

q: Bar-top apps are at 13 minutes. Who do you flag first?
why: Runner, then busser, then server, then manager — and talk to the guest about the delay. Never hope they didn't notice.
src: SERVICE.house.barsteps: "Apps down in under 12 minutes — past that, flag a runner, then busser, then server, then manager. And TALK to the guest about the delay; never hope they didn't notice."

q: Running a table's soup-and-salad course, when do you pour the soups?
a: Only once all the salads are trayed
w: While the salads are being built
After the salads have been dropped
why: Soup skins over while salad waits. Tray every salad first, then pour, then go — hot soups still get served first at the table.
src: SERVICE.house.back: "Pour soups only when the salads are all trayed — soup skins over if it sits." / SERVICE.trainer.parts[Soup, Salad & Bread Service]: "Hot soups take priority and are served first regardless of gender."

q: Which tableside show belongs to the BACK server?
why: Bananas Foster and the tower pasta are the back's shows. The smoke is yours to lift at the table, the A5 is a manager's, the Esso Affo is poured by the front.
src: SERVICE.flow[Work with your back server]: "Bananas Foster AND the tower pasta are the BACK server's shows. The +$3 smoke: bartender builds it, YOU smoke it under the lid on your tray and lift the lid at the table." / SERVICE.house.mise[Tableside shows]: "A5 / porterhouse: ... a manager slices" / BOOK Day 9: Esso Affo "shaken by the bartender, poured tableside by the FRONT server."

q: Busy night, you drop the check alongside the desserts. What do you say?
a: "This is going down here for your convenience; anything else at all, we will update it."
w: "Great question — let me find out for you."
"Let me get that closer to perfect for you."
why: The check rides with dessert on busy nights — it buys serious time, and that line keeps it from feeling like a rush.
src: SERVICE.house.front: "Busy nights: check printed and in the presenter, dropped with desserts — 'This is going down here for your convenience; anything else at all, we will update it.'" / SERVICE.house.back: "Have the check ready to drop WITH desserts on busy nights — it buys you serious time."

q: Two women ordered salads; the man at seat 2 ordered French onion. Which plate goes down first?
w: Whichever is closest to the pivot
why: Ladies first under normal service — but hot soups are served first regardless of gender.
src: SERVICE.trainer.parts[Core Dining-Room Service Standards]: "Ladies are served first under normal service." / "Hot soups are served first regardless of gender."

q: Which entree gets a cocktail fork set on the rightmost side of the guest's silverware?
why: On the lobster tails the fork sits rightmost so it is the first thing the guest's hand finds — with the butter warmer lit.
src: service.json house.mise[Preset before the food ever lands]: "On the lobster tails it sits on the rightmost side of the guest's silverware, so it is the first thing their hand finds." / mise[Twin South African Lobster Tails]: ["Cocktail fork"]; mise[FarBuckle Filet]: ["Tongs"]

q: Which starter rides out with a spatula?
why: Spatula is for the crab cake and seared scallops. Meatballs take a serving spoon, calamari tongs, goat cheese a spreading knife.
src: service.json house.mise[Starters]: "Spatula: crab cake, seared scallops." / "Serving spoon: prime meatballs, creamy spicy crab dip." / "Tongs: calamari, wagyu tacos."

q: Goat Cheese Spread: besides setting the spreading knife, what do you do at the table?
a: Drizzle the honey from the boat
w: Set off the dry-ice smoke with hot water
Pour the hot chocolate from the boat
Offer cracked pepper from the mill
why: Spreading knife plus a boat of honey — the honey drizzle is finished tableside over the crostini.
src: service.json trainer.parts[6. Appetizer Service Standards]: "Goat Cheese Spread — Spreading knife + boat of honey; honey drizzled tableside" / mise[Goat Cheese Spread]: "honey drizzle goes on at the table"

q: Baked potato lands with the steak. What do you do at the plate?
a: Cut it open, press it apart, leave the small knife in it
w: Scoop it over the steak with the big spoon
Split it in the kitchen, butter and sour cream on the side
Set it down with tongs and a ketchup ramekin
why: Cut it open and press it apart at the plate to show the steam, knife left in the potato, butter and sour cream alongside.
src: service.json house.mise[Steaks and entrees]: "Bread knife goes into the baked potato after you cut it open and press it apart." / house.mise[Sides]: "Baked potato: small knife in the potato, butter and sour cream alongside." / book Day 4: "cut it open and press it apart at the plate to show the steam, little knife left in the potato"

q: Which steak gets the Kobe Hanzo knife preset instead of a traditional steak knife?
why: Standard steaks and even off-menu cuts like the Spinalis get the traditional knife; the A5 gets the specialized Hanzo knife.
src: service.json house.mise[Preset before the food ever lands]: "Steak knives get preset for steaks. The A5 and the porterhouse get the special Kobe Hanzo knives." / trainer.parts[7. Dinner & Steak Service]: "Standard steaks — Traditional steak knife"; "Spinalis — Traditional steak knife; off-menu cut"

q: Which is NOT part of the FarBuckle setup you carry out?
why: FarBuckle: skillet, tongs, gloves, tray, rosemary salt, beef tallow, warm butter. The honing iron belongs to the A5/porterhouse block.

q: Walking behind someone with a full tray, you say…
why: Communicate every time you're moving with full trays or glassware — 'pardon my reach' is for the guest's space, not the aisle.
src: HOUSE.handbook[Safety — the nine rules]: "Say 'BEHIND YOU.' Every time. Communicate when you're moving with full trays or glassware."

q: A guest wants a cocktail-style reception for about 110 people. Which rooms could handle it?
why: Both big rooms do 125 cocktail-style — Smockton 70 seated/125, Curry 72 seated/125. The Lounge is 25 seated, the Vault 15.
src: ROOMS: "The Smockton — 70 seated / 125 cocktail-style"; "The Curry (semi-private) — 72 seated / 125 cocktail-style"; "The Lounge (semi-private) — 25 seated"; "The Vault — 15 seated"

q: A regular asks about a private dinner for 12. Which room is the smallest fit, and how many does it seat?
why: The Vault is the smallest fully private room at 15. Point them to Lillian to book it.
src: ROOMS: "The Vault — 15 seated"; "The Lounge (semi-private) — 25 seated"; "The Curry (semi-private) — 72 seated / 125 cocktail-style"; "The Smockton — 70 seated / 125 cocktail-style" + HOUSE_FACTS[Who runs the building]: "Lillian Speedy handles HR and books the banquets."

q: Wait staff uniform: which piece do YOU buy rather than the house providing it?
why: The house provides the oxford, vest and tie; you bring black pants, socks and black non-slip shoes — no tennis shoes. Checked before every shift with your crumber.
src: HANDBOOK[Look the part — conduct + dress code] Wait staff: "provided white oxford, black vest, black tie; you buy black pants, socks, black non-slip shoes (no tennis shoes); checked before every shift with your crumber — no exceptions."

q: Which of these passes the jewelry rule in the dress code?
w: A necklace worn outside the shirt
why: Basic, not extravagant: one ring per hand, up to three bracelets, earrings in ears only, no pins on vests, necklaces inside the shirt.
src: HANDBOOK[Look the part — conduct + dress code] Jewelry: "basic, not extravagant — one ring per hand, up to three bracelets, earrings in ears only, no other visible piercings, no pins on vests, necklaces inside the shirt."

q: A guest asks what's happening here Halloween night, 10/31. What do you tell them?
a: Spooky Soirée in the Lounge — live music from Greg & Steve and a costume contest
w: The Prisoner five-course wine dinner at $150 per person
Cowgirls & Cosmos in the Lounge with Christina & Frank
Chicas, Cheetahs & A Cause — $10 martinis for Hands of Hope
why: Saturday 10/31 is the Spooky Soirée: music, costume contest, drink specials. Reservations 317.641.0720.
src: EVENTS[Spooky Soirée] d: "10/31", when: "Sat · the Lounge": "live music (Greg & Steve), a costume contest, and sinfully good drink specials. Reservations 317.641.0720." (Prisoner dinner is d: "9/17"; Cowgirls & Cosmos d: "9/24"; Chicas, Cheetahs & A Cause d: "10/22")

q: End of the night, heading to your car…
a: Never walk alone — tell a manager and take the escort
w: It's fine once the lot clears
why: Handbook safety rule: nobody walks to their car alone. Tell management you're leaving and take the escort.
src: HOUSE.handbook[Safety — the nine rules]: "NEVER walk to your car alone. Tell Management you're leaving and take the escort."

q: Gift cards are sold…
a: At the BAR TOP — not the host stand
why: Send gift-card buyers to the bar, not the host stand.
src: SERVICE.flow[Desserts]: "Gift cards live at the BAR TOP, not the host stand — send buyers to the bar."

q: Ladies Night is…
a: Every Thursday in the lounge — $10 martinis and half-off apps
w: Every Thursday in the lounge — half-off martinis, $10 apps
Every Sunday in the lounge — $10 martinis
why: A weekly feature — know the martini builds and push the dessert cocktails after.
src: SPECIALS_ON[Ladies Night — every Thursday]: "Ladies get $10 martinis and half-price appetizers in the lounge, every Thursday night."

q: A guest wants to book a private dinner. Who handles it?
why: Lillian handles HR and books the banquets. Wine dinners and private rooms mean banquet money.
src: HOUSE_FACTS[Who runs the building]: "Lillian Speedy handles HR and books the banquets."; HANDBOOK[Complaints, open door + grievances]: "Lillian Speedy, our Director of Human Resources — Lillian@mosgreenwood.com"

q: You want to swap a shift with a coworker. Who can approve it?
why: Schedule posts by Wednesday for the following week — you own every shift you're on until the GM signs off on a switch.
src: HANDBOOK[Hours, the schedule + the clock]: "The schedule posts by Wednesday for the following week. Shift switches are approved by the General Manager ONLY."

q: Server uniform (men) is…
a: Black vest, black tie, white shirt, black pants, black shoes
w: Black oxford, bistro apron, two crumbers, two black pens
Long black bistro apron and black neck tie
Provided hat and t-shirt, slip-resistant shoes
why: Vest, tie and white oxford are provided; you buy the black pants, socks and non-slip shoes. Checked every shift with your crumber.
src: HOUSE_FACTS[Uniform]: "Men: black vest, black tie, long white shirt, black pants, black shoes."

q: The Vault seats how many?
why: Smockton 70 seated / 125 cocktail, Curry 72 / 125, Lounge 25, Vault 15.
src: HOUSE.rooms: "The Vault — 15 seated"; "The Lounge (semi-private) — 25 seated"; "The Smockton — 70 seated / 125 cocktail-style"; "The Curry (semi-private) — 72 seated / 125 cocktail-style"

q: Employee meals and the off-duty discount are…
a: Limited menu 50% off after your shift; 25% off food for you + 4 guests, Mon–Thu
w: Full menu 50% off any time, on or off duty
Limited menu 25% off after your shift; 50% off Mon–Thu with guests
Free limited menu after every shift; no off-duty discount
why: Enjoy your own restaurant — the 25% is the food portion only, Monday through Thursday.
src: HANDBOOK[House rules]: "Employee meals: a limited menu at 50% off after your shift … Off duty, you and up to four guests get 25% off the food portion, Monday through Thursday."

q: The progressive discipline ladder is…
a: Verbal warning → written warning → termination; on record 6 months
w: Written warning → suspension → termination; on record 12 months
Verbal → verbal → written → termination; on record 6 months
Verbal warning → written warning → termination; on record 12 months
why: Serious offenses skip steps. Theft, fighting, being under the influence, illegal acts and drugs are immediate termination.
src: HANDBOOK[Probation + discipline]: "first violation — verbal (or written) warning · second — written warning · third — termination … Violations stay on your record for six months."

q: New-hire probation runs…
why: During probation a single rule violation can end it — either side can walk for any reason.
src: HANDBOOK[Probation + discipline]: "Everyone's first 120 days are probationary"

q: Paychecks come…
a: Every other Wednesday — pay period runs Wednesday through Tuesday
w: Every Friday — pay period runs Monday through Sunday
Every other Friday — pay period runs Wednesday through Tuesday
The 1st and 15th — pay period runs by calendar month
why: A discrepancy? Tell management immediately so the next check fixes it. Someone else picks it up only with your signed note and their ID.
src: HANDBOOK[Getting paid]: "Paychecks come every other week; the pay period runs Wednesday through Tuesday, and checks are ready for pickup on Wednesday."
